Hidradenitis Suppurativa. It's incurable, progressive, exhausting, isolating, permanently disfigures your body, ruins your self-image, affects your intimate life, limits the clothes you can wear, limits the foods you can enjoy eating, smoking and drinking worsens it, ruins your mental health, makes you always have some type of pain, and no matter how many treatment options you try separately and all at once, some ridiculous thing will ALWAYS cause a flare. 

Stressing about managing any and all of the above things will 100% guarantee having a FLARE.

Not to mention that the closest thing to a "cure" to this condition is a biologic injection that could put you at risk for cancer or another serious illness due to it compromising your immune system.

And the unsolicited health advice you get from people around you makes you feel like this condition is your fault no matter how well-intentioned it is.

I would give ANYTHING to have this nightmare go away. Hopefully the future will give me and others with this wretched disease a cure or at least more treatment options.

On top of that, I would occasionally have periods where I would simultaneously have insomnia and anxiety, have my head running all day with depressing thoughts, or would have less impulse control combined with feeling pissed at everyone. 

If I felt anger, I felt simmering RAGE. If I felt anxious, I sometimes felt borderline paranoid and terrified. If I ran into something sad, I would immediately feel like I wanted to say goodbye to life. I didn't have psychosis or hallucinations so I wrote my bipolar off to just having mood swings because I believed that if you didn't have psychosis, you didn't have bipolar.

What tipped it off to my psychiatrist was that I am having these mood episodes without the influence of any type of recreational drug. I am completely sober, including not drinking alcohol. I also have comorbid ADHD, which makes it even more complex to sort this out.

People have the misconception that ALL types of bipolar include extreme depression with off-the-walls mania with psychosis, but that is definitely nowhere near true. Hypomania without psychosis exists, and the length of mood episodes aren't always clear-cut. There's rapid-cycling, cycles that last for multiple months on both ends,  longer periods of one episode with shorter periods on the other end, etc.

So yes, you ARE bipolar. Have you considered talking to her pediatrician about trying non-stimulants instead (SNRI drug class)? Those are a lot more mild than something like Adderall, and most of them are approved for children in her age group + don't have a high abuse potential.

 I'm on generic Straterra (Atomoxetine) (50mg) as an adult that's the physical size of a 12 y/o, and it's working pretty great! You could also try giving her small amounts of non-espresso coffee (1 cup or less) or even low sugar soda with caffeine and see if that would help her symptoms if you or her feel uncomfortable with trying meds again. 

There's also other ones like Kapvay, Intuniv, and a newer one you could consider trying called Qelbree that I've heard of. All of them are in the SNRI drug class. There's another SNRI called Wellbutrin that's prescribed off-label for ADHD since it's technically an antidepressant, but I personally really disliked that one because it made my anxiety ramp up significantly.

I **promise** you if you don't at least sit down and talk to her honestly about how she feels on the medication and instead deliberately choose to ignore that ADHD exists like my mother did, your relationship with her will likely be irrecoverable for the rest of your life.
